faqs.question: What are the early signs of Parkinson's disease?
faqs.answer: Early signs include a subtle tremor in one hand (often at rest), reduced arm swing when walking, stiffness, smaller handwriting (micrographia), loss of smell, softer or hoarse voice, and decreased facial expression. If you notice these, consult Dr. Lahre for evaluation.

faqs.question: Is Parkinson's disease treatable?
faqs.answer: While there is no cure for Parkinson's disease yet, excellent treatments are available to manage symptoms effectively. Medications like levodopa can dramatically improve movement, stiffness, and quality of life. Dr. Lahre optimizes treatment for each stage of the disease, helping patients maintain independence and function for many years.

whatIsIt: Parkinson's disease is a gradually progressive neurological disorder that directly impacts physical movement. It develops when dopamine-producing nerve cells in a specific brain region (the substantia nigra) begin to deteriorate and die. Because dopamine is the vital chemical messenger responsible for smooth, coordinated movements, its loss leads to the hallmark signs of Parkinson's: persistent tremors, body stiffness, slow mobility, and balance problems. While most commonly diagnosed in individuals over 60, early-onset Parkinson's can occur. Though currently incurable, expert management at Palamu Neuro & Eye Care helps patients maintain their independence and a high quality of life for many years.
symptoms: Involuntary shaking or tremors, typically beginning in the hands or fingers while at rest
Bradykinesia, which is a noticeable slowness in performing everyday tasks
Muscle rigidity and stiffness that limits the body's natural range of motion
Difficulties with balance and posture, leading to a higher risk of falls
A distinctive shuffling walking pattern and episodes of 'freezing' before stepping
Changes in handwriting, which often becomes smaller and more cramped (micrographia)
A reduction in facial expressions, sometimes called a 'masked' face
Softer, monotonous, or slurred speech patterns
Additional non-motor symptoms such as loss of smell, sleep disturbances, constipation, and mood changes
causes: Degeneration of dopamine-producing brain cells
The buildup of abnormal protein clusters (Lewy bodies) within neurons
Genetic mutations, which account for a small percentage of cases
Prolonged exposure to certain environmental toxins and pesticides (frequently seen in agricultural areas of Jharkhand)
Advancing age, with the majority of cases appearing past the age of 60
Gender factors, as men are statistically more prone to developing the disease than women

whatIsIt: A cataract is a progressive clouding of the eye's naturally clear crystalline lens. This lens is responsible for focusing light onto the retina, much like a camera lens. When proteins in the lens clump together and become opaque, light cannot pass through properly, leading to foggy, blurry, or dim vision. While cataracts are a standard part of aging—affecting a large majority of older adults—they can also be accelerated by factors like diabetes, smoking, and extensive UV exposure, a common issue for outdoor workers in Jharkhand. Fortunately, modern cataract surgery is one of the most successful and routine medical procedures available today.
symptoms: Gradually blurring, dimming, or foggy vision that cannot be fixed with new glasses
Significant difficulty seeing clearly in low light or at night, especially when driving
Heightened sensitivity to bright lights, glare, and oncoming headlights
The appearance of 'halos' surrounding light sources
A frequent need to change eyeglass or contact lens prescriptions
Colors appearing faded, washed out, or distinctly yellowish
Experiencing double vision in a single eye
Requiring much brighter lighting to read or do close-up work
causes: The natural aging process, causing lens proteins to degrade over time
Uncontrolled diabetes, which speeds up cataract formation
Long-term exposure to ultraviolet (UV) sunlight without proper eye protection
Tobacco smoking and excessive alcohol intake
Prior trauma to the eye or past intraocular surgeries
Extended use of corticosteroid medications
A strong family history of early-onset cataracts
Underlying health issues like high blood pressure and obesity

faqs.question: What is glaucoma and why is it called the 'silent thief of sight'?
faqs.answer: Glaucoma is a group of eye conditions that damage the optic nerve, usually due to elevated intraocular pressure. It is called the 'silent thief of sight' because it typically causes no symptoms in early stages — peripheral vision is lost so gradually that patients often don't notice until significant damage has occurred. Regular eye exams are the only way to catch it early.

faqs.question: Can glaucoma be cured?
faqs.answer: While glaucoma cannot be cured, it can be effectively managed to slow or halt progression. With consistent treatment (medicated eye drops, laser, or surgery), most people with glaucoma maintain useful vision throughout their lives. Early diagnosis is key — vision already lost to glaucoma cannot be recovered.

faqs.answer: Palamu Neuro & Eye Care offers comprehensive glaucoma evaluation including intraocular pressure measurement (tonometry), optic nerve examination (ophthalmoscopy), OCT imaging of the optic nerve and retinal nerve fiber layer, and visual field testing (perimetry).

faqs.question: How often should I be checked for glaucoma?
faqs.answer: Adults over 40 should have glaucoma screening every 1-2 years. Those with risk factors (family history, diabetes, high myopia, African or Hispanic ancestry, previous eye injury, or steroid use) should be screened annually. If you have been diagnosed with glaucoma, follow-up is typically every 3-6 months.

whatIsIt: Glaucoma encompasses a group of severe eye conditions that progressively damage the optic nerve, which is essential for transmitting visual signals from the eye to the brain. This damage is most often linked to abnormally high fluid pressure inside the eye (intraocular pressure). Known as the 'silent thief of sight,' open-angle glaucoma typically presents no early warning signs. It slowly erodes peripheral vision before affecting central sight. Because vision lost to glaucoma is permanently gone, early detection through routine eye exams at our Palamu clinic is absolutely critical to halting its progression and preserving your sight.
symptoms: A slow, unnoticeable loss of peripheral (side) vision in the early to moderate stages
Advanced stages resulting in narrow 'tunnel vision'
In cases of acute angle-closure glaucoma (a medical emergency): sudden and severe eye pain
Nausea, vomiting, and intensely blurred vision during an acute attack
Seeing distinct halos around lights accompanied by a red, swollen eye
Note: Primary open-angle glaucoma rarely shows any symptoms until irreversible damage is done
causes: High intraocular pressure (IOP) resulting from poor drainage of the eye's aqueous fluid
A strong genetic link (risk is significantly higher if a parent or sibling has the disease)
Advancing age, particularly for individuals over 40 and even more so over 60
High levels of myopia (nearsightedness) or hyperopia (farsightedness)
Past eye injuries, traumas, or complex eye surgeries
Chronic use of corticosteroid medications in any form
Systemic health conditions including diabetes, high blood pressure, and poor cardiovascular health
Having a naturally thin central cornea, which affects pressure readings

diagnosticTests.name: OCT (Optical Coherence Tomography)
diagnosticTests.description: High-resolution imaging of the optic nerve head and retinal nerve fiber layer — the most sensitive test for detecting early glaucomatous damage and monitoring progression.

diagnosticTests.name: Visual Field Testing (Perimetry)
diagnosticTests.description: Maps your complete field of vision to detect and quantify any vision loss from glaucoma, essential for monitoring disease progression.

diagnosticTests.name: Fundus Photography
diagnosticTests.description: Detailed color imaging of the optic nerve for documentation and serial comparison over time to detect subtle changes.

methods.name: Laser Interventions
